title: JSON printed by tools/rcon.mjs
$comment: Hand-written, for the output of tools/rcon.mjs only — it describes no server.json key and no game behaviour. Two variants, and `oneOf` because they are disjoint: `result` is the single object a one-shot run prints with --json, `shellLine` is one line of the NDJSON that `shell --json` (or the `.json` toggle) prints per command. The shell line is deliberately not composed from `commandResult` with an allOf: additionalProperties:false in a subschema would reject the host/port/clientId a sibling subschema declares. The examples that must match this schema live in skills/arma-reforger-rcon/SKILL.md, tagged with an <!-- rcon-json: … --> marker, and tools/check-rcon-schema.mjs validates them plus a few mutations that have to fail — so the document, the schema and the tool cannot drift apart silently.

ack.description: The server's 0x01|seq answer to a command packet. An acknowledgement is not a success signal: the server sends it even for a command it ignores.

logout.description: The @logout the run ended with, when one was sent.

player.description: One row of #players: the playerId, the identity id (the UID, which is what a ban needs) and the name.

bans.description: The parsed #ban list answer, including the page it came from: the server states the page count nowhere else. RCON shows 25 bans per page.

commandResult.description: One command inside `result.commands`. The shell prints the same fields plus the three that say where it is connected — see shellLine, which repeats them because of additionalProperties.

command.description: What was sent to the server, verbatim.

seq.description: The sequence number used; null when nothing was sent because the client's own grammar rejected the command.

messages.description: The raw 0x02 messages of this command, in order. The tables printed for a human are built from these, and the parsed values appear beside them.

players.description: Present only for #players, and empty when nobody is connected.

bans.description: Present only for #ban list, and only when the server sent a list — `Server has no bans to list.` is an answer, not an empty list.

error.description: The answer that made the command a failure, the client's own grammar message, or null.

exitCode.description: 0 ok, 2 usage, 4 no answer, 5 the server reported a failure.

shellLine.description: One line of the JSON that `shell --json` or the `.json` toggle prints per command. One object per command and nothing else on stdout: the banner, the notes, the prompt and the `> command` echo go to stderr.

result.description: The one object a one-shot run prints with --json, and nothing else on stdout. `players` and `bans` repeat what `commands[]` parsed, for a caller that does not want to walk the array.

command.description: The commands of the run joined with ` && `.

messages.description: Every message of the session, including `Logged In! Client ID: #N`.

loggedOut.description: True when @logout was sent and acknowledged; the slot is then free at once instead of after the 45-second timeout.
